# Brewing tea at home

A short, self-contained document for live smoke runs: small enough that one
compile takes minutes and costs cents, with enough structure to produce more
than one page. Written for this repository and released under its licence.

## Water temperature

Green tea is best brewed with water between 70 and 80 degrees Celsius. Black
tea tolerates water that has just come off the boil, between 90 and 100
degrees. Water that is too hot draws out bitter compounds from delicate leaves,
so green tea suffers first when the kettle is not left to cool.

A simple way to cool boiled water without a thermometer is to pour it into a
second cup and wait about two minutes. Each transfer between cups lowers the
temperature by a few degrees.

## Steeping time

Green tea needs one to three minutes. Black tea needs three to five. Oolong
sits between the two, and many oolongs can be steeped several times, each
steep a little longer than the last.

Steeping longer than recommended rarely makes tea stronger in a pleasant way.
It mostly makes it bitter, because the compounds that dissolve last are the
harsh ones.

## How much tea to use

A good starting point is two grams of loose leaf for every 200 millilitres of
water, roughly one teaspoon per cup. Large, open leaves take up more room for
the same weight, so a heaped spoon of them may still be the right amount.

Adjust one thing at a time: change the amount of leaf, the temperature or the
steeping time, but not all three at once, or it is hard to tell which change
made the difference.

## Storing tea

Keep tea in an airtight container away from light, heat, moisture and strong
smells. Green tea loses its fresh character within a few months once opened;
black tea keeps well for a year or more.
